summary: Describes the community package workflow: features and fixes land in collection repos with changelog fragments, minor releases every four weeks, and a cutoff that fixes which collections and majors go into the next release. Unmaintained releases normally get no fixes.
questions: Where should I contribute a fix for a module in the Ansible package?
Will an old unmaintained Ansible package version get a fix for my bug?
How are collections chosen for a new Ansible package release?
Who maintains the collections in the Ansible package?

answer_card.title: Ansible community package development workflow
answer_card.answer_md:
- Features and fixes are made in the individual **collection repositories**, following each collection's contributing rules, each with a changelog fragment.
- A minor release of the current version ships every **four weeks**.
- At the end of a cycle, release engineers announce which collections and major versions go into the next release; nothing new is added after that.
- Unmaintained releases generally get no fixes, with occasional exceptions for critical issues.

Collections are maintained by the Ansible team, partners or community teams.
